name: rndAbout
description: Composable vocabulary for generating realistic-sounding, strategically meaningless CEO marketing speeches about software and technology.
openers: I’m incredibly excited to share where we’re heading next.
Today marks an important moment in our journey.
Over the past few years, we’ve learned something fundamental about technology.
I’ve been thinking a lot about what the next chapter of software looks like.
There’s a shift happening in technology that is bigger than any single product.
The conversation around technology is changing.
We’re entering a new era of how businesses think about software.
One thing has become increasingly clear to me.
The future of software isn’t about doing more for the sake of doing more.
Something interesting is happening across the industry.
As technology continues to evolve, so does the way we think about value.
This is one of those moments where the old playbook starts to feel insufficient.
The last twelve months have reinforced something we’ve believed for a long time.
I want to take a step back and talk about the bigger picture.

leadershipLessons: Leadership isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about creating the environment where the right questions can emerge.
The best technology doesn’t replace human judgment. It gives people more context with which to exercise it.
Innovation is rarely about a single breakthrough. It’s about creating the conditions for breakthroughs to compound.
The companies that win won’t necessarily be the ones with the most technology. They’ll be the ones that know how to turn technology into leverage.
Transformation is not a destination. It’s an operating mindset.
The future belongs to organizations that can adapt faster than their environment changes.
Complexity is inevitable. Unnecessary complexity is a choice.
Technology creates possibility. Leadership determines what we do with it.
The real competitive advantage is not access to technology. It’s the ability to operationalize it.
The most valuable innovation often happens between teams, systems, and disciplines.
Speed matters, but direction matters more.
The goal isn’t to automate everything. The goal is to make better use of human potential.
Great products solve problems. Great platforms create possibilities.
Scale without alignment creates noise. Scale with alignment creates momentum.
The future is built by people willing to challenge assumptions while staying grounded in outcomes.
humbleBrags: There’s a lot more work ahead of us.
We certainly don’t have everything figured out.
We’re fortunate to be building alongside an incredible community.
The opportunity is much bigger than any one company.
We remain relentlessly focused on the problem, not the hype.
We’re proud of the progress, but even more excited about what remains unsolved.
We’ve made progress, but we’re nowhere near done.
Our team continues to surprise me with what’s possible.
We’re keeping our heads down and continuing to build.

not automation for automation’s sake, but meaningful leverage
not another tool, but a new way of working
not incremental improvement, but compounding value
not replacing people, but amplifying people
not chasing trends, but building durable capabilities
not optimizing yesterday’s workflows, but enabling tomorrow’s
not another layer of software, but an intelligent foundation

future: I believe we’re only beginning to see what’s possible.
The next phase will be even more interesting.
We’re excited to keep pushing the boundaries.
The next generation of software will be defined by how well it adapts to context.
We’ll continue investing in the fundamentals while keeping an eye on what’s next.
The companies willing to embrace this shift will have a meaningful advantage.
This will reshape how teams think about software.
We’re entering a period of extraordinary experimentation.
The boundaries between technology and the business will continue to disappear.
The real transformation is still ahead of us.
I’m optimistic about what this means for the industry.
closers: The future is being built now.
There’s never been a more exciting time to build.

requirements: Mention the selected technology at least once.
Use at least one corporate noun.
Use at least one action verb.
Use at least one vague business outcome.
Avoid concrete technical claims unless explicitly supplied by the caller.
Avoid specific facts that would require verification.
Prefer abstract outcomes over measurable details.
Sound confident without making falsifiable claims.
End with an optimistic statement or leadership sentiment.
